stop-loss.title: What's a stop loss?
stop-loss.when: The first time you open the order panel

body.p1: A stop loss is the price where your trade closes automatically if you turn out to be wrong. You choose it before you get in, while your head is still cool.
body.p2: Put your SL where your idea is proven wrong, for example just beyond support or resistance, not at a number that feels comfortable.
body.p3: In Stage 1, every trade must have an SL and a TP. After that you can trade without them, but Disiplin still checks.

risk-per-trade.title: Why risk per trade matters
risk-per-trade.when: The first time your risk goes above {max}% of your balance

body.p1: Risk per trade is the share of your balance you lose if your SL is hit. The limit here is {max}%.
body.p2: At {max}% risk, ten losses in a row still leave you about 80% of your balance. At 10% risk, five losses already take almost half of it.
body.p3: Cut the lot size or move your SL somewhere that makes sense. Don't stretch your risk for one trade that feels certain.

reward-risk.title: Reward : risk
reward-risk.when: Your first trade without a take profit (Stage 2 and up)

body.p1: Reward:risk compares the distance to your TP with the distance to your SL. A minimum of {minRR} means your target is at least {minRR}× your risk.
body.p2: Without a TP you can't tell whether the trade is worth it. A good ratio keeps you going even when you're right less than half the time.

revenge-trading.title: Revenge trading
revenge-trading.when: The first time a trade is flagged as revenge

body.p1: Revenge trading is getting back in with a bigger lot soon after a loss, here within {window} candles, to “win back” the loss.
body.p2: That decision comes from emotion, not from the chart. After a loss, pause for a candle or two, then ask: is the setup really there?

stop-out.title: What just happened: stop out
stop-out.when: The first time your account hits a stop out

body.p1: Your equity fell to {stopOut}% of the margin in use, so every trade was closed automatically to keep your balance from going negative.
body.p2: It's a sign your position was too big for your balance. A smaller lot gives you room to be wrong without losing control.

disiplin-score.title: How the Disiplin score works
disiplin-score.when: When your first Disiplin result comes in

body.p1: Every closed trade is checked: SL set at entry, risk under the limit, a TP with enough reward, SL not moved away, and not a revenge trade.
body.p2: A trade's score = checks passed divided by the number of checks. Your account's Disiplin is the average of your last {rolling} trades.
body.p3: XP only comes from Disiplin. Profit or loss adds no XP: a losing trade that followed its plan still counts.
